explain.say: Imagine a country where the emperor wears the crown, but a general really gives the orders. That was Japan for nearly 700 years. The timeline shows the age of shoguns and samurai. Let's start at the left.

explain.say: Look at the first dot. In 1192 the emperor gave Minamoto Yoritomo the title shogun, which means great general. From then on, shoguns ran the country, while emperors stayed honoured in Kyoto. Why might a general keep the emperor?

explain.say: Now look at the chain. Below the shogun were daimyo, powerful lords with land and castles. Each daimyo kept samurai, warriors who swore loyalty to him. Farmers grew rice and paid taxes in rice. Can you see who served whom?

explain.say: See the samurai? They followed a code of loyalty, courage and self-control, later called bushido, the way of the warrior. Many samurai also practised calligraphy, poetry and the tea ceremony. Surprised that warriors wrote poems?

faq.a: Shogun means great general. From 1192 to 1868 shoguns were Japan's real rulers, governing in the emperor's name while the emperor kept a mostly ceremonial role.
Powerful lords who controlled lands and castles. They promised loyalty to the shogun and kept their own samurai to defend and run their lands.
A member of Japan's warrior class who served a lord. Samurai trained with sword and bow, and were expected to be loyal, brave and disciplined.

faq.q: Why did the Mongol invasions of Japan fail?
faq.a: In 1274 and 1281 Mongol fleets sent by Kublai Khan were stopped by samurai, a long sea wall, and storms that wrecked many ships. The Japanese called the storms kamikaze, divine winds.
From 1603 to 1868 the Tokugawa shoguns ruled from Edo, now Tokyo. It was a long peace with growing cities and arts like kabuki theatre and woodblock prints, and strict limits on foreign contact.

facts: The Tokugawa shogunate ruled Japan from 1603 to 1868.
An 1876 law banned wearing swords in public, ending a key samurai privilege.

quiz.show: The real ruler of feudal Japan was…
quiz.why: Shoguns governed in the emperor's name and held the real power.

wrong.1: Farmers paid taxes; they did not rule.
wrong.2: The emperor was honoured but had little real power.

quiz.say: Who did a samurai swear loyalty to?
quiz.why: Each samurai served and swore loyalty to a daimyo.

wrong.1: The Mongols were invaders the samurai fought.
